issues.legal_issue: A High Court may not decide a second appeal on a new legal plea without complying with the requirements for identifying and hearing a substantial question of law.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court concurrently found that the plaintiff had title and that the defendants had not established tenancy rights.
The defendants raised for the first time in the second appeal a plea that the plaintiff’s vendor’s interest had vested in the State because she was not in possession on the vesting date.
The High Court accepted the new plea and dismissed the suit, but the record did not show that it formulated a substantial question of law or gave notice of such a question to the opposing party.
issues.conclusion: The High Court acted illegally and in excess of its jurisdiction by entertaining the new plea without following the mandatory procedure for second appeals. Its judgment and decree were set aside, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100(1) and (3)–(5) of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, a second appeal can be heard only on a substantial question of law, which the High Court must formulate; the respondent must be allowed to argue that no such question is involved. Under the proviso to Section 100(5), the High Court may hear another substantial question of law only after recording reasons and giving the opposing party a fair opportunity to meet it. A new case or issue unsupported by the pleadings or evidence and not raised below is generally not permissible in second appeal, except for a jurisdictional issue, and a mere question of law is insufficient. The Court relied on Panchugopal Barua v. Umesh Chandra Goswami for the requirements under amended Section 100, and referred to Sir Chunilal V. Mehta and Sons Ltd. v. Century Spinning and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd. v. Union of India for guidance on what constitutes a substantial question of law.

rule.if: second_appeal and new_legal_plea_unraised_below and (question_not_formulated or (question_formulated_late and (reasons_not_recorded or fair_opportunity_not_given)))

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal to a High Court from an appellate decree of a subordinate court.
predicates.new_legal_plea_unraised_below: A party advances a new legal plea in the second appeal that was not raised in the pleadings or before the lower courts.
predicates.question_not_formulated: The High Court does not formulate a substantial question of law for the second appeal.
predicates.question_formulated_late: The High Court formulates a substantial question of law only at a later stage of the appeal.
predicates.reasons_not_recorded: The High Court does not record reasons for deciding a substantial question that it formulates at a later stage.
predicates.fair_opportunity_not_given: The opposing party is not given a fair opportunity to address the substantial question formulated at a later stage.
predicates.second_appeal_decision_invalid: The High Court’s decision in the second appeal is legally invalid.

issues.definition: If a second appeal raises a new legal plea not raised below and the High Court neither formulates a substantial question nor, when formulating one later, records reasons and provides a fair opportunity to respond, the resulting second-appeal decision is invalid.
